lens: The efficacy of caloric restriction is not a monolithic phenomenon but is critically modulated by ancillary interventions such as resistance training, circadian feeding alignment, and baseline metabolic state, revealing a complex interplay that challenges simplistic dose-response assumptions.
known_to_ignore: Caloric restriction extends lifespan in male C57BL/6J mice (fact 161504)
Time-restricted feeding combined with caloric restriction induces weight loss in overweight/obese individuals (fact 183811)
tensions: In obese elderly, caloric restriction alone reduces lean body mass, but adding resistance training mitigates 93.5% of this loss (fact 100758) versus a non-significant trend in strength/LBM ratio (fact 100761)

30% caloric restriction in young male mice improves glucose tolerance (fact 162990), while moderate caloric restriction in human type 2 diabetes patients yields only a 6.9% remission rate (fact 185351), highlighting species or dose disparities
gaps: The interaction between circadian alignment and caloric restriction in human populations, beyond murine models (fact 161503)
The differential effects of caloric restriction on lean body mass in non-obese adults (fact 146839) versus obese subgroups
The dose-threshold for type 2 diabetes remission with caloric restriction, as only moderate reductions are characterized (fact 185351)

theses.title: Resistance training as a countermeasure to caloric restriction-induced lean body mass loss in obese elderly: A scoping review of combined interventions
theses.rationale: Synthesizes evidence showing resistance training dramatically reduces LBM loss during caloric restriction and alters strength/LBM ratios, offering a targeted strategy for a high-risk subgroup.

theses.title: Circadian alignment synergizes with caloric restriction to extend lifespan in murine models: An evidence-gap analysis
theses.rationale: Fact 161503 demonstrates a 35% lifespan extension with circadian-aligned feeding versus 10% with caloric restriction alone (fact 161504), suggesting a key mechanistic lever underexplored in translational research.

theses.title: Subtherapeutic caloric restriction dosing and limited type 2 diabetes remission: Identifying the efficacy threshold
theses.rationale: Highlights that moderate caloric restriction (500-600 kcal/day) achieves only a 6.9% remission rate (fact 185351), while murine data show metabolic improvements (fact 162990), indicating a critical dose or species-specific gap.

reviewer_objections: Overreliance on murine models for human health implications, as seen in lifespan studies (facts 161503, 161504)
Limited sample sizes and heterogeneity in human trials, such as the 2-year study in non-obese adults (fact 146839)
